explanation: The statement 'We cite no automated pipeline or release steps' is not a headline answer and misleads: README.md:4 is a build badge linking to a GitHub Actions workflow named 'Build Latest' (workflows/latest.yml), so an automated build exists. The question asks how it is built, packaged and released, in which environments. Answer it as the code shows: MSBuild/Visual Studio, Debug and Release configurations (vbproj 18-41), version.bat stamps the git description into Version.vb before building, and an automated 'Build Latest' workflow is referenced by README.md:4. Where the workflow's steps and its release target are outside what you can read, make that part `assumed` and say so, rather than saying no pipeline exists. Drop the sentence about what you 'cite'; say what the code shows.

'The only common step is a writable-or-read-only check made when each policy source opens' is cited to Main.vb 320-330 and vbproj:55, but vbproj:55 only names the manifest file and does not show its content. The app is attached to a manifest (My Project/app.manifest, requestedExecutionLevel highestAvailable) so the operating system's elevation check runs at launch ahead of all work; the earlier version stated it. Either restore it citing the manifest's own line, or drop the 'only' claim. Also GetWritability is reported when sources open and when saving (Main.vb 626-629), not on every action.

Short of its reach. The statement says saving writes the policy file or registry, updates the version file and refreshes policy, but that holds only for the Local GPO source (PolicyLoader.vb 119-133); Per-user GPO refreshes too (143-147), while a POL file is only saved to disk (140-142), the live registry is 'already applied' (134-135), an offline user hive 'will apply when policy source is closed' (136-137), and Null is 'discarded' (138-139). Also Main.vb 628-629 skips any non-writable source yet 634 still shows 'Success.' with the status 'not writable'. State which sources do what, and say success is reported even when nothing was saved.

The risk rests on knowledge from outside the code (the April 2022 end of support date) with no externalSource labelling it. The lines show only the target version. It is also overstated: App.config 4 is a supportedRuntime of v4.0 with sku 4.5.2, so the program runs on whatever 4.x Framework is installed (README.md 33-36 says '4.5.2 or newer', and 4.8 is preinstalled on current Windows), not on a frozen 4.5.2 runtime. Add the externalSource and restate the harm at the reach the lines show, that the program is built against an end-of-support target, or drop the risk.

True that the MSI is run through msiexec with no checksum or signature check, but the statement overreaches. The download is over HTTPS from a fixed download.microsoft.com address (DownloadAdmx.vb 3), so it is not 'over the network' unverified in a way a person on the network can alter without breaking TLS; the exposure is a hash-less trust in that one host. The destination is the editable TextDestFolder (default %windir%\PolicyDefinitions, lines 18, 37), not always the Windows folder, and ownership/ACL changes (94-100, 52-75) apply only if the destination exists and the user is an administrator, and replace the ACLs of the files moved in. State the reach that way.

says: The Save command shows 'Success.' even when neither policy source was writable and nothing was written (the status text reads 'not writable'), and the save of comments is swallowed. No finding names this harm: a person who edited a read-only or non-committable source can believe the change was saved. Add a failure-handling finding for the save path, citing the lines, with its reach limited to sources whose writability check failed.

An external system is not named: the ADMX download reaches download.microsoft.com with a hard-coded installer address and a hard-coded path inside the MSI for one Windows 11 release (DownloadAdmx.vb 3-4), so the feature breaks when that file moves, and it fails with only the failed phase shown. Fold into a fact, or the failures answer, what the program reaches outside the machine.
